name: AICPA & CIMA on AI in Accounting: Guidance, Research and CPE
title: AICPA & CIMA on AI in Accounting: Guidance, Research and CPE
answer: AICPA & CIMA's site collects Insights Blog articles, CPE webcasts and courses on AI in accounting and finance. Its most useful contribution is practical guidance on how AI changes work design, adoption and controls: research on human-AI collaboration, generative AI applications for CPAs, survey findings on accountant willingness and barriers, and courses on AI agents, governance and critical thinking. Readers get a profession-body view of AI's implications for audit, corporate finance, reporting, forecasting and skills.

sections.body: AICPA & CIMA publishes this collection of professional insights articles and CPE learning pages on its website. The material includes Insights Blog posts dated June 26 2025, August 6 2025 and September 9 2026, plus webcast and course pages on AI for finance teams, generative AI and AI agents, smart adoption, and critical thinking in AI-driven decisions. The pages cover AI in accounting, audit, corporate finance, controllership, reporting, forecasting, governance and skills. The website was read on September 30 2026.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: Across the pages, AICPA & CIMA treats AI as a practical shift in how accounting and finance work is designed, governed and performed. A podcast episode with Professor Jasmijn Bol says organizations often layer AI onto existing work, but the deeper change comes when AI becomes a contributor and alters the division of labour. As AI handles structured and routine work, human value comes from interpreting information, challenging assumptions, applying context and exercising judgement. Her research found that when AI initiated an email, outputs were rated higher for overall quality, creativity and personal touch, while participants reported lower psychological ownership. Where high-quality output matters, letting AI generate a first draft can work; where ownership matters, a human draft with AI feedback may be preferable. Other pages explain generative AI for CPAs, including using ChatGPT for Excel formulas, creating macros and complex spreadsheets, explaining tax code, and supporting audit disclosures and financial analysis. A research summary cites an Ipsos UK report for Chartered Accountants Worldwide finding 85% of accountants willing to use AI and 80% expecting significant job transformation within five years, with adoption driven more by individual proactivity than organizational change. Courses cover real-world AI in reporting, forecasting, revenue recognition and process automation, the progression from chatbots to AI agents, risks, controls and governance, and critical thinking to validate AI-generated data.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The text gives several figures and positions. An Ipsos UK report commissioned by Chartered Accountants Worldwide found 85% of accountants surveyed willing to use AI and 80% believing AI will significantly transform jobs within five years. A blog post says ChatGPT reached 100 million active users a month two months after its November 2022 release. It defines machine learning as consuming data to predict outcomes, while generative AI creates new content from input. It says Deep Research can take about 20 minutes to return an answer. A course page lists Chris Gillette of Group 1 Automotive, a Fortune 250 retailer with $23 billion in annual revenue and a team of more than 700 professionals. Paid CPE access lasts three months or one year depending on product, and one course includes a 30-Day AI Plan while another includes a 90-day roadmap. Arvind Narayanan and Sayash Kapoor argue AI is a normal general-purpose technology whose integration will take decades.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in accounting would use this source to see how the profession's body frames adoption, not just tool hype. It offers research on human-AI collaboration and work design, survey evidence on accountant attitudes and barriers, practical generative AI uses for CPAs, and CPE courses on AI agents, governance, controls and critical thinking. It is useful for audit, corporate finance, reporting, forecasting and controllership roles, and for understanding skills shifts such as critical thinking, data security, AI ethics and advisory capabilities. It also gives a profession-level view of risks and oversight when scaling AI.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Accounting

sections.body: The material is a mix of blog summaries, course descriptions and promotional CPE pages, not a single research report or standard. Some pages are commercial course listings with access periods and speaker biographies. The survey findings are reported second hand through an AICPA & CIMA article, and the podcast and blog posts summarize individual research and commentary rather than setting out formal guidance. The pages do not provide a complete regulatory framework or detailed implementation methodology, and the dated posts range from 2025 to 2026.
